item.title: Limit theorems for random matrix products with a simple top Lyapunov exponent
item.description: arXiv:2610.12678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study products of independent, identically distributed random matrices with an exponential moment and a simple top Lyapunov exponent, without assuming irreducibility. Outside an exceptional invariant subspace called the equator, we establish contraction on average for a weighted projective distance and a spectral gap for the associated Markov operator. We obtain a central limit theorem, a Berry--Esseen bound, deviation estimates near the mean, and an almost sure invariance principle both for the growth of a fixed vector outside the equator and for the operator norm. For fixed vectors, a non-arithmeticity assumption also yields a local limit theorem and a renewal theorem. Our contraction criterion applies more generally to mostly contracting random maps on locally compact spaces with a Lyapunov function, including certain random interval maps.
item.dc:creator: Pablo G. Barrientos, Dominique Malicet

item.title: Pointwise H\"older continuity of Lyapunov exponents of random matrix products
item.description: arXiv:2610.12698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that if the first Lyapunov exponent of a compactly supported random matrix product is simple, then it is pointwise H\"older continuous for the Wasserstein--Hausdorff distance. By passing to exterior powers, we obtain pointwise H\"older continuity of the first $k$ exponents whenever they are simple.
item.dc:creator: Pablo G. Barrientos

item.title: Uniform Exponential Attractors for Non-Autonomous Dynamical Systems and an Application to the damped hyperbolic equation with sub-quintic growth
item.description: arXiv:2610.13068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop an abstract framework for the theory of uniform exponential attractors in non-autonomous dynamical systems. Our construction employs time-dependent absorbing sets while ensuring exponential attraction among the constructed sets. Moreover, we show that the resulting exponential attractors are uniform-that is, they remain stable under perturbations. As an application of this abstract theory, we study the weakly damped hyperbolic equation with sub-quintic nonlinearity. Using the proposed approach, we construct exponential attractors for the process generated by the Shatah-Struwe solution, which satisfies both energy and Strichartz estimates. Furthermore, we establish the Holder continuity of these exponential attractors with respect to the external forcing term.
item.dc:creator: Chang Qingquan, Li Dandan

item.title: A Lipschitz refinement of the Bebutov-Kakutani dynamical embedding theorem for connected Lie group actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected Lie group equipped with a compatible right-invariant metric and let $G$ act continuously on a compact metrizable space $X$. We prove that $X$ admits a $G$-equivariant embedding into the right argument shift action on the space of one-Lipschitz maps from $G$ to $[0,1]$ if and only if the set of fixed points topologically embeds into $[0,1]$. This generalizes a theorem proved by Gutman, Huo and Tsukamoto for $\mathbb{R}^k$-flows.
item.dc:creator: Yonatan Gutman, Qiang Huo, Kangbo Ouyang

item.title: Khintchine dichotomy for images of self-similar measures and almost random walks
item.description: arXiv:2610.13099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Following the celebrated breakthrough in B\'enard-He-Zhang, we prove Khintchine dichotomy for push-forwards of self-similar measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under uniform $C^{1+\alpha}$ maps. For this, we also study almost random walks on $\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{Z})$ and prove their effective equidistribution.
item.dc:creator: Liyang Shao

item.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses
item.description: arXiv:2610.13100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity. This settles Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane. Albouy and Kaloshin proved it for masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two. We follow their method. Infinitely many central configurations would give an algebraic curve of complex solutions. At the places at infinity of the curve the valuations of the mutual distances must balance. We determine the possible valuation vectors at all positive masses, together with the mass conditions under which each can occur. We treat limits in which four bodies form a cluster of zero potential energy by expanding the potential, which is constant along the curve, at a place. This excludes, at every positive mass, one of the two diagrams in which such clusters occur, and part of the other. The same expansion excludes one further diagram at every positive mass. What remains is an exact analysis, by computer algebra, of the sets of mass conditions that can hold together at positive masses. Exact rational certificates show that the balance fails under each of them, except on a few one-parameter families of masses, which we treat separately. On the rays through $(1,4,4,4,4)$ and $(1,1,4,4,4)$ the certificates do not apply. On the first ray they cannot apply: there the complex equations have a continuum of solutions, as Albouy and Kaloshin observed. On these rays we count the real central configurations: there are 306 and 294 up to orientation-preserving similarity. The certificates, the programs that check them and a proof of the theorem in the Lean proof assistant are available.
item.dc:creator: Tejasvi Singh Tomar

item.title: Hausdorff Dimension and Flexibility for Attractors of Non-Uniformly Hyperbolic Flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.13160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Hausdorff dimension of attracting sets of three-dimensional flows whose one-dimensional quotient dynamics is non-uniformly expanding. Our main assumption is that the quotient map admits a full-branch uniformly expanding Gibbs--Markov induced map. We first prove that every such attractor contains a hyperbolic horseshoe of Hausdorff dimension strictly larger than two. As a consequence, after an arbitrarily small $C^2$ perturbation, the associated dynamical Lagrange and Markov spectra have robustly non-empty interior for an open and dense set of $C^1$-observables. We then establish intermediate dimension properties. Every admissible intermediate Hausdorff dimension is realized by an ergodic invariant measure supported on the attractor. Moreover, every intermediate stable and unstable dimension is realized by a strictly ergodic hyperbolic subsystem. The approach extends the dimension theory previously developed for geometric Lorenz attractors to more general non-uniformly hyperbolic attractors including singular-hyperbolic attractors, Rovella attractors, and broad classes of skew-product suspension flows modeled by intermittent and Benedicks--Carleson maps.
item.dc:creator: Elias Rego, Paulo Varandas

item.title: Dimension theory of group actions by circle diffeomorphisms I: Stationary measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.13254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a structure theorem for smooth random walks on the circle and study the dimensional properties of their stationary measures, including exact dimensionality and a Ledrappier-Young-type dimension formula. These results provide the technical tools needed for the main theorems in Part II "Dimension theory of group actions by circle diffeomorphisms II: Minimal sets". They also yield an approximation theorem in the spirit of Katok, Avila-Crovisier-Wilkinson, and Morris-Shmerkin, together with a time-reversal symmetry for circle actions: every semigroup $T$ contained in $\mathrm{Diff}_+^{1+\alpha}(\mathbb{S}^1)$ without finite orbits has the same number of minimal sets as its inverse semigroup $T^{-1}$.
item.dc:creator: Weikun He, Yuxiang Jiao, Disheng Xu

item.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Discrete-Time Self-Attention Dynamics in Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2610.13518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In machine learning, a self-attention dynamics describes the attention mechanism of transformers, and is obtained treating the layer index of a transformer as time index. Even though naturally discrete-time, this dynamical system is most often studied in continuous-time. Scope of this paper is to provide a thorough investigation of the discrete-time version of the self-attention dynamics: a complete classification of its equilibria is given, and their stability properties are studied, in both the single-head and the multihead case. We show that in both cases the main attractor of the dynamics is a consensus equilibrium aligned with the principal eigenvector of the value matrix (in the single-head case, a corresponding matrix of weights in the multihead case), even though other locally asymptotically stable bipartite equilibria can be show to exist at least in the single-head situation. The behavior is confirmed by looking at the learned weight matrices of a real transformer.
item.dc:creator: Claudio Altafini

item.title: Adjoint-Based Stochastic Analysis for Fatigue of Aeroelastic and Frictional Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As engineering systems are optimized to reduce weight and improve performance, vibration behavior, including nonlinear effects, is becoming increasingly important to analyze. While methods such as harmonic balance are popular for analyzing periodic nonlinear vibration behavior, these analyses often only consider deterministic loading. However, real applications experience additional noise in the excitation, and alternative approaches are frequently limited to smaller models. This work expands on a recent approach to calculate a time-varying covariance using a linearized system around a periodic nonlinear response. Specifically, numerical conditioning is addressed and improved for cases increasing from a few degrees of freedom to hundreds of degrees of freedom. The algorithm is then extended to capture correlations across both space and time via a period-spanning covariance matrix. Model reduction is proposed for this calculation to maintain computational efficiency. The period-spanning covariance matrix is used to sample full stochastic cycles and estimate fatigue-relevant statistics up to 1393 times faster than stochastic time integration. Importantly, the present methodology uses the same gradient information as stability analyses and continuation solutions, so it can easily be applied for many nonlinear analyses. The methodology is demonstrated for two beam systems: one with unsteady aerodynamic forces and another with a Bouc-Wen frictional tip force. For the aeroelastic model, statistics are accurately estimated via the present approach. For the frictional system, some errors are introduced compared to stochastic time integration and are attributed to the linear time-periodic nature of the system used in the present stochastic calculations. However, estimated stochastic statistics remain useful given the significant reduction in computation time.
item.dc:creator: Justin H. Porter

item.title: Odd order cases of Chowla's averages over arbitrary rectangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.12869v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. In this paper we prove an average form of Chowla Conjecture for even $k $. that is, for every fixed even integer $k\geq 2$, we prove that \[ \lim_{\min\{M,N\}\to \infty}\frac{1}{MN}\sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{n=1}^N\lambda(m)\lambda(m+a_1n)\cdots\lambda(m+a_kn)=0. \] We construct a stationary model for both averaging variables, derive the finite conditional-entropy estimates. A comparison of overlapping intervals on the logarithmic axis then forces this function to vanish.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Huo, Zhengxing Lian, Kangbo Ouyang

item.title: Decomposition results for multiplicative actions and applications
item.description: arXiv:2503.15175v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by partition regularity problems of homogeneous quadratic equations, we prove multiple recurrence and convergence results for multiplicative measure preserving actions with iterates given by rational sequences involving polynomials that factor into products of linear forms in two variables. We focus mainly on actions that are finitely generated, and the key tool in our analysis is a decomposition result for any bounded measurable function into a sum of two components, one that mimics concentration properties of pretentious multiplicative functions and another that mimics vanishing properties of aperiodic multiplicative functions. Crucial to part of our arguments are some new seminorms that are defined by a mixture of addition and multiplication of the iterates of the action, and we prove an inverse theorem that explicitly characterizes the factor that these seminorms naturally determine.
item.dc:creator: Nikos Frantzikinakis

item.title: Shadowing in CR-Dynamical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2505.23089v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A CR-dynamical system is a pair $(X, G)$, where $X$ is a compact metric space and $G$ is a closed relation on $X$. We introduce four $(i,j)$-shadowing properties, obtained by independently varying the quantifiers in the definitions of pseudo-orbit and shadowing. These properties coincide with the classical shadowing property for single-valued systems, while $(2, 2)$-shadowing agrees with the established notion of shadowing for set-valued dynamical systems. We investigate how the classical characterisations of shadowing for the identity map, periodic maps and isometries extend to closed relations. In particular, we obtain rigidity results for $(2, 1)$-shadowing and positive results for $(1, 2)$-shadowing on totally disconnected spaces. Finally, whenever the infinite Mahavier product is non-empty, we prove that a closed relation has the $(2, 2)$-shadowing property if, and only if, its associated Mahavier dynamical system has the shadowing property. This removes the surjectivity hypothesis from a recent corresponding result for set-valued dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Wood

item.title: Upper bound for the number of limit cycles for symmetric piecewise linear differential equations with three zones
item.description: arXiv:2507.06705v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The study of the periodic dynamics of the family of continuous observable and non-controllable three-dimensional symmetric piecewise linear systems with three zones considered here can be reduced to the study of periodic solutions of the piecewise differential equation $x'=ax+(b-a)\mathop{\rm sat}(x)+\mu\sin t$, where $\operatorname{sat}$ stands for the normalized saturation function. This paper proves that the number of limit cycles (that is, isolated periodic solutions) of the equation is uniformly bounded independently of $a,b,\mu$. Moreover, when $ab>0$, the equation has exactly one limit cycle for every $\mu>0$. When $ab<0$, it has exactly three limit cycles for sufficiently small $\mu>0$ and exactly one for sufficiently large $\mu$. When $ab<0$, using Melnikov theory for a deformation of the equation, we prove that, for each fixed $\mu>0$ away from two critical values and for sufficiently small nonzero values of the perturbation parameter, there are exactly three, five or one limit cycles, depending on $\mu$. This strengthens the conjecture that the equation has at most five limit cycles.
item.dc:creator: J. L. Bravo, V. Carmona, M. Fern\'andez, I. Ojeda

item.title: Equidistribution of expanding translates of smooth curves in homogeneous spaces under the action of a product of SO(n,1)'s
item.description: arXiv:2511.04799v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the limiting distributions of expanding translates of a compact segment of a smooth curve under a diagonal subgroup of $G=\prod_{i=1}^k\mathrm{SO}(n_i,1)$, where $G$ acts on a finite volume homogeneous space $L/\Gamma$ as a subgroup. We show that the expanding translates of the curve become equidistributed in the orbit closure of $G$, provided that Lebesgue almost every point on the curve avoids a certain countable collection of algebraic obstructions. Building on Ratner's measure classification theorem and the linearization technique, we establish the result by analyzing polynomial approximations of the curve on shrinking intervals, using Kempf's geometric invariant theory and certain estimates on maximal eigenvalues in $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$-representations.
item.dc:creator: Yubin Shin

item.title: An inverse theorem for all finite abelian groups via nilmanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2512.17468v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a first inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all finite abelian groups that uses only nilmanifolds (rather than possibly more general nilspaces). This makes progress toward confirming the Jamneshan--Tao conjecture. The correlating function in our theorem is a projected nilsequence, obtained as the fiber-wise average of a nilsequence defined on a boundedly-larger abelian group extending the original abelian group. This result is tight in the following sense: we prove also that $k$-step projected nilsequences of bounded complexity are genuine obstructions to having small Gowers $U^{k+1}$-norm. This inverse theorem relies on a new result concerning compact finite-rank (CFR) nilspaces, which is the main contribution in this paper: every $k$-step CFR nilspace is a factor of a $k$-step nilmanifold. This new connection between the classical theory of nilmanifolds and the more recent theory of nilspaces has applications beyond arithmetic combinatorics. We illustrate this with an application in topological dynamics, by proving the following result making progress on a question of Jamneshan, Shalom and Tao: every minimal $\mathbb{Z}^\omega$-system of order $k$ is a factor of an inverse limit of $\mathbb{Z}^\omega$-polynomial orbit systems of order $k$, these being natural generalizations of nilsystems alternative to translational systems.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Candela, Diego Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez, Bal\'azs Szegedy

item.title: Lyapunov exponents for random products of non-negative matrices
item.description: arXiv:2602.23317v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We first study i.i.d. products of finitely many invertible $2 \times 2$ matrices with positive entries, and prove that the top Lyapunov exponent admits an explicit, rapidly convergent Neumann-series-type representation involving an infinite matrix. We further show that non-negative invertible $2 \times 2$ matrices are simultaneously conjugate to positive matrices if and only if ``generalized'' heteroclinic connections do not occur among products of length at most $2$. These results yield a series formula for the Hausdorff dimension of the intersection of the middle-$n$th Cantor set with a random translate of itself, for every natural number $n$ except $4$. Furthermore, our method applies to the intersection of thick Cantor sets under random translation. We also determine the almost sure growth rate of i.i.d. three-term recurrences with finitely many positive coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Nima Alibabaei

item.title: Why does entropy drive evolution equations?
item.description: arXiv:2603.07653v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: `Entropy' appears as driving force in many different evolution equations, both deterministic and stochastic, and in these equations this `entropy' also takes different forms. We show how all these examples can be understood as different instances of a common principle: Entropy drives evolutions because it characterizes the invariant measure of an underlying stochastic process. This interpretation explains the appearance of entropy, the different forms that entropy takes in these equations, and how entropy `drives' these evolution equations. We illustrate this common structure with examples from stochastic processes, gradient flows, and GENERIC systems.
item.dc:creator: Mark A. Peletier

item.title: Surfaces with nonpositive magnetic curvature
item.description: arXiv:2608.13534v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a negatively curved surface, magnetic (or twisted geodesic) flows with nonpositive ''magnetic curvature'' have a large-scale geometry on the universal cover that retains some features associated with geodesic flows: magnetic boundary and visibility, possibly magnetically flat strips. This has dynamical consequences: orbit-equivalence to the geodesic flow, density of periodic points, transitivity, entropy-expansivity, existence of equilibrium states.
item.dc:creator: Boris Hasselblatt, JinCheng Wang

item.title: On the Finiteness of Anosov flows on $3$-manifolds via Contact Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2609.03700v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In dimension 3, following Eliashberg-Thurston and Mitsumatsu, one can associate a transverse pair of oppositely oriented contact structures to any Anosov flow. We show that when the ambient manifold is hyperbolic, the isotopy classes of these contact structures completely determine the flow up to isotopy orbit equivalence. This then implies that on any closed hyperbolic 3-manifold, the number of Anosov flows modulo isotopy orbit equivalence is finite. This approach also yields an explicit bound on the number of orbit equivalence classes of Anosov flows in terms of the number of universally tight contact structures. In addition, we show finiteness of pseudo-Anosov flows for which the complement of the singular orbits is atoroidal and, in the non- hyperbolic case, we obtain a control on the dynamics of Anosov flows on the hyperbolic pieces of the JSJ-decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Bowden, Vincent Colin

item.title: Relative ($\tau$), Expanders, and Decay of Correlations for certain Expanding Maps
item.description: arXiv:2609.05271v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Relative ($\tau$) is equivalent to a statement that the sequence of Cayley graphs associated to group quotients $\Gamma_q=\Gamma/N_q$, $q\in\mathbb{N}$, form an expander family. There is a philosophy that expander graphs give rise to good mixing; for instance, one has exponential mixing for the geodesic flow uniformly the along a family of congruence covers of the modular surface, stemming from the symmetry in the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ action and the uniform spectral gap for the Laplacian. Do we see similar phenomena in less structured settings? We investigate this question for a tower of finite sheeted covers of certain expanding dynamical systems. We use transfer operator machinery that applies in particular in the cases of subshifts of finite type and expanding interval maps. We make fruitful connections with KMS states of Cuntz--Krieger algebras.
item.dc:creator: Rhiannon Dougall

item.title: Dynamic Bifurcation of Nonautonomous Evolution Equations: Invariant Manifold Methods
item.description: arXiv:2609.08107v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we use the global invariant manifold and the reduced singular cohomology groups method, which is different from those in the literature, to study the dynamic bifurcation from infinity of the nonautonomous evolution equation in terms of invariant sets by applying the Conley index theory (due to Rybakowski). We first establish a nonautonomous global invariant manifold for the abstract equation, which allows us to reduce the original system to this finite-dimensional manifold. Then, a homotopy between the reduced equation and a product flow is constructed. Finally, by considering the reduced singular cohomology theory of the Conley index, we establish our main theorems on dynamic bifurcations from infinity for this nonautonomous equation. As an example, a nonautonomous parabolic equation on unbounded domains is considered. Some new detailed results on bifurcations from infinity of the parabolic equation under an appropriate Landesman-Lazer type condition are proved, including the existence of a nonautonomous Morse decomposition, and improving the earlier works in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Chunqiu Li, Jintao Wang

item.title: A strict amplitude lower bound for the van der Pol equation and extensions to symmetric Li\'enard systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.27305v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the amplitude of the unique limit cycle of the van der Pol equation $\ddot{x}+\mu(x^2-1)\dot{x}+x=0$ is strictly greater than $2$ for every $\mu>0$. The proof combines orbit comparison in the relaxation oscillation regime, trigonometric comparison curves in the weakly nonlinear regime, and polynomial energy estimates in the intermediate regime. The polynomial sign conditions arising in the latter two regimes are certified using exact rational arithmetic and Bernstein coefficients. The orbit comparison method also applies to a class of symmetric Li\'enard systems. Under suitable monotonicity assumptions, we establish a sufficient criterion for the limit cycle amplitude to exceed a critical value determined by the damping function.
item.dc:creator: Changjian Liu, Ziwei Zhuang

item.title: Threshold Geometry, Bifurcation, and Data-Driven Analysis of a Vaccination-Treatment Model for Hepatitis B
item.description: arXiv:2609.39204v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite the availability of excellent vaccines and antiviral medicines, hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major public health problem. In this work, we develop a mathematical vaccination-treatment model for HBV transmission to investigate threshold conditions for illness persistence as well as the level of intervention. The analysis gives the characterisation of both disease-free and endemic equilibria and determines the basic reproduction number, $\mathcal{R}_0$, by the next-generation matrix approach. The model indicates that $\mathcal{R}_0=1$ is a critical threshold dividing disease-free from endemic states and characterises a forward transcritical bifurcation regarding the transmission parameter. Numerical equilibrium continuation and stability assessments confirm the analytical results. A two-parameter study of transmission and vaccination rates identifies threshold geometries and assesses impacts of important parameters using sensitivity analysis. The model is calibrated with India-specific data, such as HBsAg prevalence, HBV incidence and mortality rates and fits epidemiological targets closely through limited nonlinear calibration. Additionally, multi-start optimisation and practical identifiability profiling are used to investigate parameter uncertainty. Robustness analyses reveal that the calibrated $\mathcal{R}_0^*=1.1744$ is associated with a super-threshold regime; however, parameter flexibility permits both sub-threshold and super-threshold regimes. This combined analytical and data-driven framework connects epidemic thresholds, bifurcation structures, intervention efficacy, and parameter uncertainty. It provides a quantitative framework for analysing HBV persistence and evaluating control options, especially in the absence of epidemiological evidence.
item.dc:creator: Mustaq Ahmad, A. S. Bhadauria

item.title: Strict Hausdorff-dimension drop for Quartic Salem Bernoulli convolutions
item.description:
arXiv:2610.12072v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every quartic Salem number $ eta$, we prove that the equal-weight Bernoulli convolution $
u_{ eta^{-1}}$ has Hausdorff dimension strictly less than one. The main step converts large Fourier coefficients at geometrically separated frequencies into a deficit in the Shannon entropy of a finite convolution. A positive trigonometric product gives the entropy estimate, while the algebraic norm controls the number of distinct atoms in each spatial cell. For the two quartic Salem numbers in $(1,2)$, reciprocal differences at suitable return times produce the required Fourier coefficients. A finite block cover then gives the dimension bound. This proof is independent of numerical computation. Separate exact calculations give $\dimH
u_{ eta_1^{-1}}<1-1.4\cdot10^{-23}$ and $\dimH
u_{ eta_2^{-1}}<1-7.8\cdot10^{-22}$, where $ eta_1< eta_2$ are the two parameters in $(1,2)$. The accompanying verification programs use rational interval arithmetic and the Python standard library.
item.dc:creator: Guozheng Cheng, Xiang Fang, Xueqing Ma, Hongli Zhang

item.title: $J$-class weighted translations on locally compact groups
item.description: arXiv:2506.04730v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A bounded linear operator $T$ on a Banach space $X$ (not necessarily separable) is said to be $J$-class operator whenever the extended limit set, say $J_T(x)$ equals $X$ for some vector $x\in X$. Practically, the extended limit sets localize the dynamical behavior of operators. In this paper, using the extended limit sets we will examine the necessary and sufficient conditions for the weighted translation $T_{a,\omega}$ to be $J$-class on a locally compact group $G$, within the setting of $ L^p$-spaces for $ 1 \leq p < \infty $. Precisely, we delineate the boundary between $J$-class and hypercyclic behavior for weighted translations. Then, we will show that for the torsion elements in locally compact groups, unlike the case of non-dense orbits of weighted translations, we have $J_{T_{a,\omega}}(0)=L^p(G)$. Finally, we will provide some examples on which the weighted translation $ T_{a,\omega}$ is $J$-class but it fails to be hypercyclic.
item.dc:creator: A. R. Imanzadeh Fard, M. R. Azimi, I. Akbarbaglu
